name: The Venerable Oak of the Botanical Garden

location.address: Conservatoire et Jardin botaniques de Genève, near the Avenue de la Paix entrance

verified_sources: https://sitg.ge.ch/arcgis/rest/services/SIPV_ICA_ARBRE_ISOLE (SITG cantonal isolated-tree inventory, no_inventaire 19800587I0, circumference 710cm, vitality Médiocre, stage Sénéscent)
access: Free, open garden during opening hours
transport: Tram to Nations or the botanical garden stop, then a short walk
verify_notes: Named 'Vénérable Vieux Chêne Pédonculé' by the City of Geneva's own 'Graines de curieux' museum-trail article, which gives inventory number XX0G19800587, exactly matching the register's no_inventaire 19800587I0 for the same coordinates: a genuine cross-source match, not a guess. The article dates it to 1719 (article itself written/updated with an 'en 2021' reference giving ~300 years old at that time, so roughly 305-307 today) and says it once bordered a Roman road that passed through the site before the botanical garden existed. Called the 'doyen' (elder) of the garden's living collection. A quiet 'périmètre de tranquillité' (protective perimeter) has been set around it to stop soil compaction from foot traffic, which the article gives as the reason its Médiocre/Sénéscent status in the register is being actively managed rather than ignored. Register also confirms it is alive (status Relevé) with a recent observation. Roughly 450m from the already-published Botanical Garden Plane Trees (gen_004), a different specimen inside the same garden complex, easy to combine into one visit. Flagged only because age is derived/approximate rather than a precise archival date; existence, species, location and history are all corroborated by two independent city sources.

name: The Naville Cedar

location.address: Route de Frontenex, opposite no. 53, Villereuse

verified_sources: https://sitg.ge.ch/arcgis/rest/services/SIPV_ICA_ARBRE_ISOLE (SITG cantonal isolated-tree inventory, no_inventaire SEVE_231592, circumference 722cm, vitality Bon, planted 1820-01-01)
access: Free, stands at the roadside, visible and reachable at any time
transport: Bus to Frontenex or a 15-20 minute walk from the centre
verify_notes: Tribune de Genève's 'Ces arbres remarquables qui racontent Genève' names this exact tree: planted in summer 1820 by Jean-Edouard Naville, mayor of Eaux-Vives, on his Montchoisy estate, to mark the birth of his son Emile. The article places it 'across from number 53, Route de Frontenex', which matches the register coordinate precisely (situation: Bords de voie / roadside) and the register's own planted date of 1820-01-01. Note the register's own '01-01' date-trap caveat applies to this date in principle, but here it is independently corroborated by a named, dated historical account (a real event, a real family, a real month even if the day is not recorded), which is exactly the case where BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's trap does not apply: a source says THIS tree was planted in 1820, not merely that the district was landscaped around then. The article calls it strong despite standing 'in the middle of concrete', consistent with the register's Sénéscent development stage but Bon vitality. A good stand-alone stop or a short detour from the Grange/Eaux-Vives cluster, about 450m from the already-published Grange Cedar (gen_003).

verify_notes: The City of Geneva's own didactic walking guide 'Promenade du Parc la Grange au Parc des Eaux-Vives' lists 21 named trees worth stopping for along this exact route, including 'Cyprès chauve - Parc des Eaux-Vives (n147/144)' among its 'arbres insolites' (unusual trees), independently confirming a bald cypress is one of the park's officially signposted specimens; the register gives the only individual tree in this species within the park at these coordinates, Excellent vitality, girth 330cm. About 320m from the published Grange Cedar (gen_003), inside the same lakeside park complex, and a natural addition to that walk with a genuinely different silhouette (conifer that drops its needles, a rarity for the walk).

location.address: Parc de l'Impératrice, Chemin de l'Impératrice 10

verified_sources: https://sitg.ge.ch/arcgis/rest/services/SIPV_ICA_ARBRE_ISOLE (SITG cantonal isolated-tree inventory, no_inventaire SEVE_285081, circumference 506cm, diameter 161cm, vitality Bon)
access: Free, public park, open at any time (the city bought the estate in 1983; the château itself now houses Italy's UN mission, but the grounds and lawn are public)
transport: Bus toward Chambésy/Pregny, or roughly 25 minutes on foot from the botanical garden
verify_notes: Geneva's own page for Parc de l'Impératrice names 'un tulipier de Virginie splendide et un séquoia grandiose' standing together at the top of the terrace lawn that descends from the château, among the park's 'superbes arbres centenaires' (superb century-old trees); the register's single Liriodendron tulipifera entry in the park, girth 506cm, matches this description and location. The 1983 sale to the City of Geneva made the park public even though the château became the Italian Mission's seat, so despite the register's situation field reading 'Cour' (courtyard), this is public parkland, not a private embassy garden; checked specifically because 'Cour' elsewhere in this register can mean a private courtyard. Register's planted date (1912-01-01) sits in the sentinel range, so age is instead a rough girth-based estimate for a fast-growing species in generous open ground, not a documented date. About 270m from the published Botanical Garden Plane Trees (gen_004), across the railway cutting; walkable but a separate small stop rather than the same cluster.
